newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan new crop cotton rises, old crop steady.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan new crop cotton rises, old crop steady.

text.p: Pakistani new crop cotton rose on Wednesday on increased buying by textile mills, dealers at the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said.

Mills with ready cash were purchasing 1997/98 (July-June) cotton amid uncertainty about the crop size, dealer Oveis Razzak said. Pakistan has set a production target of 10 million 375-lb bales for 1997/98, up from 8.78 million produced in 1996/97.
In the kerb market, new crop of NIAB-78 variety was quoted at 2,560/2,570 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).

The KCA said exporters had shipped 142,212 bales of cotton by July 19 compared to 1.82 million on the same date a year ago. Exporters had registered contracts to export 190,080 bales by July 28 compared to 2.32 million at the same time a year ago.
